description: Caches and leftovers from everyday apps: browsers, chat, media, creative tools, updaters.

rules.name: Google Chrome browser cache
rules.reason: Web pages, images and scripts Chrome saved to load sites faster.
rules.regenerates: Chrome refills it as you browse.

rules.name: Google Chrome compiled-code & service-worker caches
rules.reason: Offline copies of websites and compiled JavaScript. Not your bookmarks, passwords or history.
rules.regenerates: Chrome rebuilds them as you visit sites.

rules.name: Old Google Chrome/Updater downloads
rules.reason: Update packages and on-device model files Chrome downloads in the background.
rules.regenerates: Downloaded again if Chrome needs them.

rules.name: Browser cache
rules.reason: Pages and images the browser saved to load sites faster.

rules.name: App updater leftovers
rules.reason: Downloaded app updates that were already installed.
rules.regenerates: The app downloads the next update when one is available.

rules.name: Desktop app web cache
rules.reason: Desktop apps built on web tech (Slack, Discord, Teams, VS Code, Notion…) keep a browser-style cache here. No messages, files or settings.
rules.regenerates: The app rebuilds it on next launch.

rules.name: Spotify offline/stream cache
rules.reason: Streaming cache Spotify keeps in ~/Library/Caches. Downloaded (offline) music lives elsewhere and is not included.
rules.regenerates: Spotify refills it as you listen.

rules.name: Zoom data cache
rules.reason: Temporary Zoom data. Your recordings in ~/Documents/Zoom are not included.

rules.name: Adobe media cache
rules.reason: Preview/conform files Premiere, After Effects and Audition generate from your media.
rules.regenerates: Regenerated when you open a project (first open is slower).

rules.name: Docker disk image
rules.reason: All Docker images, containers and volumes live in one large disk file.
rules.advice: Run `docker system prune -a` (and `docker volume prune` if you're sure) instead of deleting the file, or lower the disk limit in Docker Desktop settings.
